claim: Mitochondria are organelles that produce ATP through oxidative phosphorylation providing energy for cellular processes
The cell membrane is a selectively permeable lipid bilayer that controls the movement of substances in and out of cells
Stem cells can differentiate into specialized cell types and are capable of self-renewal through mitotic division
Epigenetics studies heritable changes in gene expression that do not involve alterations to the DNA sequence itself
RNA carries genetic information from DNA to ribosomes where it directs protein synthesis through translation
The microbiome refers to the community of microorganisms living in a specific environment such as the human gut
Telomeres are protective caps at the ends of chromosomes that shorten with each cell division and are associated with aging
Protein folding is the process by which a polypeptide chain assumes its functional three-dimensional structure
The immune system distinguishes between self and non-self through major histocompatibility complex molecules on cell surfaces
Photoreceptors in the retina convert light into electrical signals that are processed by the visual cortex of the brain
Synaptic plasticity the ability of synapses to strengthen or weaken over time is considered the cellular basis of learning and memory
The blood-brain barrier is a selective membrane that protects the brain from pathogens and toxins while allowing essential nutrients to pass
Circadian rhythms are approximately 24-hour cycles in biological processes regulated by the suprachiasmatic nucleus in the hypothalamus
Antibiotic resistance develops through natural selection when bacteria with mutations survive antibiotic treatment and reproduce
The human body contains approximately 37 trillion cells organized into tissues organs and organ systems
Type 2 diabetes results from insulin resistance and relative insulin deficiency often associated with obesity and sedentary lifestyle
Immunotherapy harnesses the body own immune system to fight cancer by enhancing or restoring immune function
Gene therapy treats disease by modifying or replacing defective genes within a patient cells
The gut-brain axis describes bidirectional communication between the gastrointestinal tract and the central nervous system
Herd immunity occurs when a sufficient proportion of a population is immune to an infectious disease reducing its spread
Biofilms are structured communities of microorganisms attached to surfaces that are highly resistant to antibiotics and immune responses
CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing has been used to treat sickle cell disease in clinical trials by modifying patient blood stem cells
Neuroplasticity allows the brain to reorganize neural pathways and form new connections throughout life in response to experience
Prions are misfolded proteins that can cause other proteins to misfold leading to progressive neurodegenerative diseases
The lymphatic system transports lymph fluid filters pathogens and plays a critical role in immune function
